sections.html: Lonchogenys ilisha is an extremely unusual tetra and a member of the family Acestrorhynchidae, which means the species is more closely related to the barracuda tetras (Acestrorhynchus) than, for example, to a cardinal tetra. The maximum length reported is 6-7 cm; the imported specimens were 5-7 cm long and most probably almost fully grown.
Lonchogenys ilisha is the only known member of its genus. It occurs in the upper and middle Rio Negro region in Brazil and Colombia. The imported specimens originate from Colombia.
First observations showed the species to be very peaceful, both towards conspecifics and towards other fish of similar size.
Specimens with a golden shine and a bright orange caudal fin are thought to be the males.
No information is available so far regarding the aquarium biology of this species.
